newsitem.title: FRANCE: French truckers' unions and bosses set talks.
newsitem.headline: French truckers' unions and bosses set talks.

text.p: Truckers' unions and haulage bosses were due to begin talks at 4:30 p.m. (1530 GMT) on Thursday to discuss how to end a four-day protest that has blocked roads across France, a union official said.

Michel Caillaud of the National Federation of Truck Drivers said he was not certain whether the discussions would address the unions' main demands on wage increases, retirement at 55 instead of 60 and shorter working hours.
"What they are ready to discuss does not necessarily correspond to our demands," Caillaud said.

The employers' Union of Transport Federations agreed late on Wednesday to negotiate with the truckers' unions. But the protests intensified on Thursday and began to show signs of squeezing the economy.

Car maker PSA Peugeot Citroen said that it reduced shifts at several plants because of a shortage of spare parts. Some supermarkets and petrol stations were running low on supplies because of the protests.
Motorways in and out of some 30 cities across the country were barricaded with Bordeaux, Toulouse, Lyon, Clermont-Ferrand, Caen and Le Mans among the most severely hit.
